clue.text: Try harder to draw nose broken by punches before winning

explanation.surface: A boxer drawn into a bout gets a broken nose from the punches before finally winning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges NOSE to ONES; the possessive apostrophe of ONE'S is not shown in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: to stop slacking and make a greater effort, which is what trying harder means.

clue.text: Group filming soldier coming down hill

indicators.note: in a down clue the soldier comes first, above the hill

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper
a mount is a hill or mountain, as in Mount Etna

explanation.surface: A film crew shoots a paratrooper descending a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: Paramount Pictures is a Hollywood studio, a company that makes films.

clue.text: Found cold tea horrible

indicators.note: a horrible mess of the letters is a reshuffling

explanation.surface: Someone discovers that their cold cup of tea is awful.
explanation.definitionFit: Having found something is having pinpointed where it is, a past-tense synonym.

clue.text: Female, first of two ladies in extra large clothing

indicators.note: the woman and the letters go inside the size abbreviation

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, a clothing size
Vera is a woman's name

indicators.note: the initial letter is taken twice over
the opening letter of ladies

explanation.surface: A woman and two others wear oversized garments.
explanation.walkthrough: OS (outsize) is the clothing-label size abbreviation; 'first of two ladies' means the L of ladies taken twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Overalls are protective work garments worn over other clothes.

clue.text: Finish your meal with some Costa espressos

parts.note: the run TAE sits across cosTA Espressos; the answer read as an instruction, its first word written up, gives that run, and some says only part of these words is used

explanation.surface: Telling someone to clear their plate along with a few coffees from the chain.
explanation.walkthrough: Costa is a British coffee chain. cosTA Espressos holds TAE, which is the answer's first word written up, as a down light enters it: the answer itself supplies the hiding and the turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrasal verb telling someone to consume everything on their plate.

clue.text: Actor's way-out and eccentric, so great when holding party

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hold the party word inside
eccentric letters are odd, so they are rearranged

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: An actor who is way-out and eccentric is so great when hosting a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' rearranges SO GREAT to STAGEOR; 'holding' puts DO inside. 'way-out' looks like a synonym for eccentric but means exit.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre's performers' exit to the street is their own way out, the familiar backstage door.

clue.text: "My soldiers, my companions" (The Queen)

parts.note: cor is an exclamation like 'my!' of surprise
GIs are American soldiers

explanation.surface: A monarch's speech praising her troops as her companions.
explanation.definitionFit: Elizabeth II famously kept Welsh dogs as pets, constant animal companions.

clue.text: "Who is Zoë Ball?" starts reverberating where she works

indicators.note: letters reverberating are shaken about into a new order
the opening letters of the presenter's two names

explanation.surface: A quiz question about the British TV and radio presenter Zoë Ball, with echoes of the answer.
explanation.walkthrough: Zoë Ball is a British broadcaster. 'starts' gives Z and B, and 'reverberating' rearranges them with WHO IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Entertainment as an industry, the world in which a TV and radio presenter makes her living.

clue.text: Like 3, 13 and 17, in first of poems by Frost

indicators.note: the opening letter of poems

parts.note: rime is hoar frost, ice crystals on surfaces

explanation.surface: Reading poems by Robert Frost, looking at numbered pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frost' looks like the poet, but it is rime.
explanation.definitionFit: Three, thirteen and seventeen are each divisible only by one and themselves, so they share that number property.

clue.text: Most smutty erotica's sadly loveless

indicators.note: something done sadly is done badly, so the letters are thrown into a new order
love is zero in tennis scoring, shaped like the letter O, and the word says that letter goes

explanation.surface: A complaint that the dirtiest erotic fiction is, regrettably, without any romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loveless' takes O (love, the tennis zero) out of EROTICAS, leaving ERTICAS, which 'sadly' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Racy writing is risqué, so the superlative describes the most indecent or bawdy material.

clue.text: Article by monk, one deduced

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
a prior is a monk who heads a priory
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A religious newsletter piece written by a monk, someone who reasoned it all out.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin phrase for knowledge reasoned from first principles rather than observed, so it describes something worked out by deduction.

clue.text: Encountered some turbulent air

indicators.note: to air something is to bring it into view, so the answer is exposed inside these two words

explanation.surface: A pilot reporting that the flight ran into a patch of rough air.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across soME Turbulent; 'air' is the best candidate for the indicator, since 'some' is part of the text the letters come from.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: having come across someone is having encountered them, both past tense.

clue.text: Paper round gets Puck into Telegraph? That's significant

indicators.note: the word Paper is turned round into a different order
Puck's letter goes into the telegraph word

parts.note: a cable is a telegram, a message sent by telegraph
Puck is the setter, who refers to himself as I

explanation.surface: A paper round gets the setter a job at the Daily Telegraph newspaper, a big deal.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often call themselves I; 'Telegraph' looks like the British newspaper but means a cable, a telegram.
explanation.definitionFit: Something large enough to notice or matter is appreciable, a near synonym of considerable or significant.

clue.text: Wave excessively, shortly before getting it on with a fresher

indicators.note: shortly means the synonym is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: unduly means excessively, more than is fitting

indicators.note: a fresher form of the letters is a new arrangement of them

explanation.surface: Someone waves far too eagerly before getting it on with a first-year university student.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' trims UNDULY to UNDUL; 'fresher', which looks like a British first-year student, rearranges IT ON plus A into ATION.
explanation.definitionFit: A wave is a rising and falling movement, which is exactly what an undulation is.

clue.text: Male who's on the up as a speculator

parts.note: Theo is a man's name
a riser is someone who is rising, going up

explanation.surface: A man whose career is climbing as a market gambler.
explanation.definitionFit: One who speculates in the sense of forming hypotheses, rather than the financial gambler the surface suggests.

clue.text: Book, the last written in a long time

indicators.note: the last letter is written inside the word for a long period

parts.note: an era is a long period of time
Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A book's final word, penned over many years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written in' puts Z, the last of the alphabet, inside ERA.
explanation.definitionFit: Ezra is a book of the Old Testament, so the name stands for a book of the Bible.

clue.text: Air traffic controller that's first leaving 20?

definitions.meaning: the system that steers an aircraft automatically controls air traffic in a humorous sense
20's first name alone is pilots' slang for the automatic flight system

explanation.walkthrough: 20 is the footballer and airport; taking his surname off leaves George, pilots' nickname for the automatic flying system.
explanation.definitionFit: The automatic flight-control system flies the aircraft, so it controls traffic in the air.

clue.text: Springer? He might add some spice

definitions.meaning: spring is a season, so one who deals in seasons is jokingly a springer
someone flavouring food with salt, herbs or spices

explanation.walkthrough: 'Springer' looks like a spaniel or a jumper, but spring is one season of the year.
explanation.definitionFit: A cook who flavours dishes is someone who seasons them.

clue.text: Model to order online in great volume

parts.note: the Model T was Ford's early car, so T can stand for the model
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
e- as in email or e-commerce marks something done online

explanation.surface: An instruction to order a model kit online in large quantities.
explanation.definitionFit: A tome is a large, heavy book, so a great volume in the bookish sense rather than loudness.

clue.text: An excellent conductor of energy in a storm, perhaps

indicators.note: energy's letter goes inside the rearranged letters
perhaps flags the words as one possible arrangement of the letters

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A lightning rod in a storm, an excellent conductor of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges A STORM; 'in' puts E inside, giving MAESTRO. 'conductor' looks electrical, but it is musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian for master, used for a distinguished conductor of an orchestra.

clue.text: Pilot, one who ran over time getting to airport

parts.note: George is pilots' slang for an aircraft's autopilot

indicators.note: over means the name is turned the other way round

parts.note: Seb Coe, the British Olympic middle-distance runner

explanation.surface: A pilot, a former runner, races against the clock to reach the airport.
explanation.walkthrough: Seb Coe is the British Olympic middle-distance champion. Belfast's airport is George Best City Airport, named after the Northern Irish footballer.
explanation.definitionFit: Belfast City Airport is officially named after the footballer, so his name is used for the airport.

clue.text: Former prime minister's missing a head of uniformed force out

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: the name is missing the named letters

parts.note: Pierre or Justin Trudeau, prime ministers of Canada

indicators.note: the first letter of uniformed

explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' removes A and U (head of uniformed) from TRUDEAU, leaving TRUDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To extrude is to thrust or push something out, as metal is pressed through a die.

clue.text: Boot the filth found by chance, we hear

indicators.note: we hear marks a word spoken, so the spelling follows the sound

parts.note: muck is filth and luck is chance, side by side

explanation.surface: Kicking the dirt that turned up accidentally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'filth' looks like British slang for the police, but here it is muck.
explanation.definitionFit: A mukluk is a soft sealskin or reindeer-hide boot worn by Arctic peoples.

clue.text: He sees Trump bad for women as a group

indicators.note: letters in a bad state are jumbled, so these words are reordered

explanation.surface: A man finds Donald Trump harmful to women's interests.
explanation.definitionFit: The Motown act was a female vocal trio, a group made up of women.

clue.text: Covers fish up

indicators.note: in a down light, up means the word is written from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: a sprat is a small fish

explanation.surface: An order to cover the fish and bring them up.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for tarpaulins, the waterproof sheets used to cover things, plural noun.

clue.text: Short version of the greatest piece for former boy band member

parts.note: Muhammad Ali called himself the greatest; shortened, his name is M. Ali
K is the king, a chess piece

explanation.surface: An abridged version of a top hit made for an ex-pop-group singer.
explanation.walkthrough: Zayn Malik left One Direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Zayn Malik sang with One Direction before going solo, so he is an ex-member of a pop group.

clue.text: Bring to an end, removing the head!

definitions.text: Bring to an end, removing the head!

indicators.note: the first letter of the synonym is taken off

parts.note: to stop something is to bring it to an end

clue.text: A 19's baby's toys

explanation.walkthrough: 19 is MAESTRO; the first reading treats a conductor's name, Simon Rattle, as a type, with the 's read as a plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakers given to infants that make noise when moved are the familiar baby's toys.

clue.text: Line gut with ale, missing last bits of speech

indicators.note: missing says letters are dropped from the three words before them
the final letter of each of the three words

explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' takes away the 'last bits', the final E, T and E of LINE, GUT and ALE.

clue.text: Farm animals changed direction, with rain starting to hit area just south of London

in cricket a ball that broke changed direction off the pitch

parts.note: to belt is to hit hard

explanation.walkthrough: The stockbroker belt is the affluent commuter country of Surrey and nearby counties, where City financiers live.
